title: Transformer thermal loading and ageing
card_detail: IEC 60076-7 hot-spot model, EV hosting capacity and insulation ageing.
context: A 630 kVA 20/0.4 kV ONAN secondary-substation transformer feeding 180 households with rooftop PV and a growing number of electric vehicles. Hot-spot and top-oil temperatures follow the IEC 60076-7 loading-guide thermal model, insulation ageing follows the guide's relative-ageing law, and every case is checked against the normal cyclic loading limits. Thermal parameters are typical ONAN values and the load, PV, EV and weather profiles are synthetic study assumptions.

statement.tool: Python implementation of the IEC 60076-7 thermal model (difference equations) and ageing law
statement.built: Steady-state and dynamic hot-spot model, EV, PV and battery scenarios, and a 0-200 EV hosting-capacity sweep
statement.result: Shifting EV charging to the night cut insulation ageing on a 160-EV winter day by 98.6 %

flow_label: Profiles to thermal model to ageing to limit check
flow: top oil and hot spot, 1 min steps
method_note: In winter the 1.5 pu current limit binds before the hot-spot limit: the cold ambient keeps the hot spot at 109 °C even at 1.72 pu. The battery therefore adds 30 EVs of capacity, while shifted charging removes the evening peak altogether.

results: 160 EVs uncontrolled, 200+ with battery or shifted
1.72 pu peak, 108.8 °C hot spot, 0.135 days of life
1.10 pu peak, 65.7 °C hot spot, 0.0019 days of life
decisions: Simulate three identical days and keep the last, so results do not depend on the starting temperature.
Count reverse PV flow as transformer loading, since the windings heat in either direction.
Report which limit binds, not only whether a case passes, because the remedy differs.
Keep thermal parameters as stated assumptions until fitted to a real heat-run report.
verification: 11 tests: rated-load temperatures, dynamic model settling on the steady state, oil time constant, ageing law at 92, 98 and 104 °C, upgraded-paper reference, one day of life at 98 °C, EV energy conservation, battery limits and the hosting-capacity boundary.
